batch_strategy: Use the latest rejected strong-eluent humps to test remaining response-shape boundaries, while preserving scaffold-specific exceptions. Add targeted loading and protocol comparisons, two reference repeats around m92's latest failure, and strong-condition labels where the endpoint predictions become narrowly separated or inverted.

choices.reason: m127 in pure EA at 163.5 mg still predicts completion at 18.65 mL, above measured same-loading 1/1 and 2/1 completions of 10.13 and 12.27 mL in 5b1af559138d20cb2423 and f4e1a820726cf8f5d4e2. This tests whether the rejected 1/1 hump has left an unsupported maximum at the strongest boundary.

Acetylfluorene m38 in pure EA at 100 mg predicts 3.27/14.30 mL. The same-loading 2/1 reference a2f5638c0f2528673e4e measured 4.82/12.63 mL. This independently tests a predicted strong-boundary reversal on a fused aromatic carbonyl graph; it complements the selected lower-loading pair without conflating their loadings.

m38 at 1/1 and 50 mg predicts completion at 18.72 mL, versus 12.54 mL for the selected loading-matched 2/1 row. Recent m180 and m127 1/1 labels rejected analogous maxima. This tests whether that repair transfers to an acetyl group attached to fluorene.

m38 at 2/1 and 50 mg completes the controlled 1/1-to-2/1 comparison. Its predicted 5.40/12.54 mL is close to the middle-loading reference a2f5638c0f2528673e4e, while measured middle-loading 5/1 record 7b341f30a27433562690 finished at 20.87 mL. The pair locates the strong transition rather than extending a common carbonyl offset.

Fluorenone m182 in pure EA at 90 mg predicts completion at 10.13 mL, before the measured same-loading 1/1 completion of 17.95 mL in d6f36b5de45565d68603. This anchors a potentially genuine sharp strong-condition transition that differs from the recently measured compact cyclic ketones.

m182 at 2/1 and 90 mg fills the gap between d6f36b5de45565d68603 at 1/1 and bc3692f55b839d2f2c07 at 5/1, which finished at 17.95 and 21.80 mL. The predicted 4.78/18.20 mL tests whether this rigid cyclic ketone really has a longer strong-region completion baseline than m179 and m180.

Bromobenzofuran m8 at 2/1 and 235.95 mg predicts completion at 17.94 mL, above same-loading 5/1, 20/1 and 50/1 measurements bb387f1af7263b2445fb, 5806c857509e09634010 and 12aed585647de3f03908, all near 16 mL. This tests the remaining strong-region maximum in a heteroaromatic ether rather than assuming the carbonyl repair applies.

Ether-containing aldehyde m59 at 2/1 and 58.1 mg predicts completion at 19.96 mL, above its measured 5/1 completion of 14.31 mL in 6209df8dd01072ab8a47. This tests a different location of the recurring predicted maximum, with the selected 10/1 row bounding its continuation.

m59 at 10/1 and 58.1 mg predicts 11.56/17.68 mL. Together with selected 2/1 and measured 5/1 record 6209df8dd01072ab8a47, it supplies a fixed-loading segment that distinguishes an isolated 2/1 overshoot from a broader scaffold-specific response. Middle-loading weak references f5d802ca42b1a7226fc0 and 85591a54c419ed02c5f5 constrain the larger-volume region.

Dimethylbenzaldehyde m134 at 2/1 and 96.2 mg predicts completion at 17.40 mL, above the selected 5/1 prediction of 15.97 mL. Measured same-loading 10/1 record c8b332c6c452d13fcc6e finished at 16.80 mL. This tests whether the nearly flat strong segment recently measured for trimethylacetophenone extends to an aldehyde with a different steric environment.

m134 at 5/1 and 96.2 mg completes the matched 2/1-to-5/1 comparison. The measured 10/1 and 50/1 records c8b332c6c452d13fcc6e and 8b06ec38a7e5999edfa6 provide surrounding anchors. Although the predicted decrease is modest, both new labels identify response shape on an otherwise uncovered strong segment.

Methyl anthranilate m104 at 1/1 and 58.4 mg predicts completion at 12.28 mL, above its selected 2/1 prediction. Ethyl anthranilate actually decreased from 11.40 to 9.69 mL in 4849c7e8a804b692efb7 and 6fe6280def3960fa4f99. This tests a chemically meaningful exception to the recently rejected neutral-carbonyl humps.

m104 at 2/1 and 58.4 mg completes the matched amino-ester pair, predicting 5.21/9.97 mL. Same-loading 5/1 reference 9333d130f52d80332cf0 measured completion at 13.75 mL. These labels test whether the ethyl ortho-amino ester's local decrease transfers to the methyl ester under its recorded DCM protocol.

Para-amino ethyl benzoate m86 in pure EA at 175.5 mg anchors its uncovered strongest boundary against same-loading 1/1 record 4d3b1628cd2311585f50, completion 15.08 mL. The latest meta-isomer pure-EA completion was 12.77 mL in 425074f6cad1ac0c1bc8. This tests positional transfer while retaining the different recorded loading protocols.

Para-aminobenzonitrile m160 in pure EA at 100 mg predicts completion at 9.56 mL, but its measured 1/1 and 2/1 references fbf7711e24f45bf06d4f and 2feb7d8e0a3566ddf97f finished at 19.81 and 33.83 mL. This tests the strong boundary of an aniline-nitrile response rather than transferring an amino-ester or pyridine baseline.

Meta-aminobenzonitrile m161 in pure EA at 100 mg matches the selected para isomer's recorded protocol. Its predicted completion of 9.54 mL is nearly identical despite distinct measured weaker responses; 0c24b9414856413c9a67 and 17902fa9c7f8ea9b456e finished at 18.76 and 84.79 mL at 1/1 and 5/1. The pair tests where positional differences emerge.

Repeat m92 at 20/1 and 115.5 mg to check the reference used to interpret the latest upper-loading failure. bbb514661c0a49694d6a measured 13.55/33.32 mL, whereas upper-loading e9dc948c0e68a88eb621 measured 5.42/21.38 mL. This repeat tests reference stability before attributing that contrast to a deterministic loading interaction.

Repeat m92 at 10/1 and 173.25 mg, matching ad0ace61c29817c678c2, which measured 8.66/29.54 mL. The latest same-loading 20/1 label e9dc948c0e68a88eb621 was earlier and smaller. This checks the neighboring reference needed to distinguish a reproducible local reversal from the recorded variability already seen at upper-loading 5/1.

m61 at 2/1 and 101.2 mg predicts 6.62/12.43 mL and supplies a stronger-condition anchor for the latest 5/1 result 994a1f65509549a84ede, onset 10.27 mL. That onset contradicted the previous broadly early-onset interpretation. This label tests whether the change is localized to the intermediate solvent segment.

m61 at 10/1 and 50.6 mg predicts an early onset of 3.86 mL. Middle-loading 859ae738b615cf17b849 measured onset at 3.04 mL, whereas the latest middle-loading 5/1 onset was 10.27 mL. This new loading boundary tests whether the early weak-region onset transfers without assuming that it applies throughout the alcohol's curve.

DCM-loaded m72 at 2/1 and 51.1 mg begins a matched recorded-protocol comparison. Lower-loading 1/1 DCM records 6a53fc46345dc50021ae and 4df0734ab058c0eeed78 differed substantially, while the latest middle-loading repeat was stable. A new condition helps test whether the lower-loading protocol association persists beyond that variable reference.

PE-loaded m72 at 2/1 and 51.1 mg matches the selected DCM row's sample loading. Lower-loading PE 1/1 record d2472f692763fd970d64 finished at 14.46 mL; middle-loading PE and DCM 1/1 records a2c9096e1ec2e5c244d6 and d90d024730eb01bff3c7 were close. This tests a regime-dependent joint solvent/volume association, not an isolated solvent mechanism.

Ethyl phenylacetate m83 in pure EA at 51.5 mg predicts 8.19/7.10 mL, an inverted endpoint order. Its strong-region evidence includes ordered middle- and upper-loading 1/1 labels 0520aee15336815a25f0 and e2848d4b338b394b93a2. This directly tests whether the model has reduced completion without appropriately adjusting onset.

m83 in pure EA at 154.5 mg supplies the loading counterpart, predicting 7.03/8.03 mL. The model changes from inverted to ordered endpoints as loading increases. Measuring both extremes teaches the density-times-volume interaction separately for V1 and V2 and prevents a single anomalous prediction from determining the entire strong baseline.

Aryl pinacol boronate m62 in pure EA at 52.5 mg predicts 7.50/6.70 mL. Same-loading 1/1 and 2/1 observations cb79e57eb461a7dcc59a and 84cd955ed2d585ae02fe had ordered endpoints. This tests the endpoint-coordination concern in a boronate environment distinct from ordinary carbonyl esters.

m62 in pure EA at 157.5 mg completes the loading-extreme comparison, predicting 6.32/7.64 mL. Both pure-EA rows are uncovered, while 899e3f4f8af9b2c20b3b measured compact completion at middle-loading 5/1. The pair tests whether the predicted onset decrease and completion increase across loading are measured.

Diiodobenzene m157 in pure EA at 50 mg predicts completion at 8.53 mL, versus 4.45 mL for selected 1/1. Its measured 50/1 reference 51b57cfd0a20117aab60 finished at 11.51 mL at 100 mg. This establishes a strong boundary on a sparsely anchored nonpolar graph after m0 and m5 strong-region overpredictions were exposed.

m157 at 1/1 and 50 mg predicts 4.95/4.45 mL, combining endpoint inversion with a deep completion minimum relative to selected pure EA. The matched pair can identify an unsupported solvent-shape feature independently of loading and constrain transfer among heavily halogenated nonpolar aromatics.

Cyclohexyl phenyl ketone m175 in pure EA at 50 mg predicts 5.15/4.88 mL. Related isopropyl phenyl ketone c260e5193159c51fe828 measured an ordered 3.68/6.83 mL in pure EA, and m175's 2/1 reference a44bda1a7abf6efee26c finished at 9.91 mL at 100 mg. This tests whether compact ketone corrections have overshrunk completion.

Chlorobenzophenone m176 at 20/1 and 50 mg establishes the fixed-loading reference for selected 50/1. Prediction is 5.87/18.40 mL, close to middle-loading observation c717afaee5336c60c59f, 4.72/18.69 mL. This makes the weaker-boundary experiment interpretable for both endpoints.

m176 at 50/1 and 50 mg predicts 11.48/34.87 mL and has the highest supplied CW-distance percentile. No measured 50/1 boundary is supplied for this scaffold. The selected 20/1 counterpart tests this growth against the very different measured weak responses of methyl-, methoxy-, cyano- and nitro-substituted benzophenones.

Dibenzoylmethane m168 in pure EA at 80 mg anchors an uncovered strong boundary, predicting 3.12/7.99 mL. Same-loading 5/1 and 10/1 records ea810ad3e836415369bd and 4c7a167609de5f3e01c2 finished at 17.05 and 20.40 mL. This tests the scope of compact strong-region learning across a beta-diketone topology rather than extrapolating from acceptor count.

hypotheses.content: The pronounced predicted 1/1 completion maxima were rejected in all four recently measured matched carbonyl pairs: m179, m180, m181 and m127 instead increased toward 2/1. This supports repairing unsupported strong-region curvature, but does not establish universal solvent monotonicity. Remaining pure-EA reversals and maxima at other strong conditions require scaffold-specific boundaries, including longer-baseline fluorenone and noncarbonyl heteroaromatics.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels at both sides of remaining response-shape features can correct shared condition representations while preserving genuine structural differences and separate onset behavior.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m127's pure-EA reversal, m38's 1/1 maximum, and the predicted m8, m59 and m134 intermediate maxima survive measurement, and where does fluorenone's longer completion baseline begin?

hypotheses.content: m92 cannot be represented by a fixed loading offset. Its latest middle-loading 50/1 completion of 61.95 mL was close to prediction and to the lower-loading 58.54 mL result, whereas upper-loading 20/1 measured only 5.42/21.38 mL against larger lower and middle references. The upper-loading 5/1 repeat also varied substantially. These observations leave a solvent-dependent loading association and unrecorded variability as competing explanations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Checking influential references can prevent one unexpectedly early, compact label from becoming an unsupported mass correction for every condition and both endpoints.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the middle-loading 20/1 and upper-loading 10/1 references reproduce, leaving the latest upper-loading 20/1 contrast localized?

hypotheses.content: m72's recorded protocol associations are condition- and loading-specific. Middle-loading DCM 1/1 completions reproduced at 20.40 and 20.50 mL, and PE loading finished nearby at 21.16 mL. Lower-loading PE finished at 14.46 mL, while exact DCM references differed between 10.60 and 20.79 mL. A large constant loading-solvent offset is therefore unsupported; solvent and loading-solvent volume also change together in this comparison.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A matched new-condition comparison can teach the encoded joint protocol association without treating variability or correlated recorded factors as a universal solvent mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At lower-loading 2/1, are PE and DCM completions close as currently predicted, or does the lower-loading 1/1 contrast persist?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing strong response shapes remain scaffold-specific. Meta-amino ethyl benzoate increased from 12.77 to 17.08 mL completion between pure EA and 1/1, whereas ortho-amino ethyl benzoate decreased from 11.40 to 9.69 mL between 1/1 and 2/1. The latter is a modest, unreplicated observed exception. Ester alkyl group, amino position and nitrile versus ester connectivity may define transfer boundaries, with recorded protocols retained as possible contributors.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These comparisons test genuine exceptions alongside failure repair, preventing a common nitrogen offset or a universal monotonic curve from replacing structure-condition learning.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does methyl anthranilate share the ethyl ortho ester's local decrease, and do para amino ester and matched meta/para aminonitriles have the predicted compact pure-EA boundaries?

hypotheses.content: The previous broadly early-onset interpretation for m61 is weakened. The new middle-loading 5/1 onset was 10.27 mL, and upper-loading pure-EA and 1/1 onsets were 5.03 and 5.72 mL. Earlier middle-loading 10/1 and upper-loading 5/1 observations still have small onsets. The pattern may be restricted to particular conditions or reflect unrecorded variability, rather than a general secondary-alcohol baseline.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: New anchors can localize onset corrections independently of completion and limit transfer of an early-onset association across alcohol conditions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does middle-loading 2/1 connect smoothly to the newly measured 5/1 onset, and does the small 10/1 onset transfer to lower loading?

hypotheses.content: Several uncovered strong rows predict extremely small or inverted V1/V2 gaps, particularly pure-EA m83, m62 and m175 and 1/1 m157. One hypothesis is that compact completion corrections have not been coordinated with onset and loading responses. Recent compact m0, m5 and m80 labels retained ordered endpoints, but supplied m73 records include inversions, so the hypothesis should be tested through labels rather than enforced as an absolute catalog constraint.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Strong-condition loading pairs and a fixed-loading solvent pair can expose which endpoint relationship needs correction across simple esters, boronates, ketones and nonpolar graphs.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the predicted inversions measured, and do m83 and m62 actually change onset and completion in opposite directions across loading?

hypotheses.content: Benzophenone weak-boundary responses require substitution-specific learning. Supplied 50/1 completions range from about 28 mL for dimethyl substitution to 76 mL for methoxy and 117 mL for cyano substitution; nitrobenzophenone records vary sharply across recorded loadings. Chlorobenzophenone's currently predicted increase from about 18 to 35 mL between 20/1 and 50/1 remains unmeasured and should not inherit another substituent's correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The matched weak segment tests structural transfer and onset/completion growth in a high-distance region despite a narrow single-predictor completion quantile span.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does chlorobenzophenone at fixed 50 mg show the predicted 20/1-to-50/1 growth, and which endpoint accounts for it?

feedback_interpretation: The latest matched carbonyl experiments strongly weakened the predicted-hump interpretation: m179, m180, m181 and m127 all had larger completion at 2/1 than at 1/1, with historical 1/1 completion overpredictions of approximately 7–10 mL. I therefore test remaining maxima and pure-EA boundaries on related but distinct graphs instead of immediately repeating their repaired segments. m29 was nearly flat between 2/1 and 5/1, reinforcing the need to learn response shape without imposing strict monotonicity. m92's middle-loading 50/1 completion was close to its acquisition prediction, reducing the value of another immediate repeat there; its upper-loading 20/1 result instead exposed a substantial failure in both endpoints and motivated checking the references surrounding that contrast. The m72 middle-loading DCM repeat reproduced completion almost exactly, and the matched PE result was close, weakening any large constant protocol-offset explanation while leaving the lower-loading comparison unresolved. m61's new 5/1 onset rejected a generally early-onset interpretation, so its follow-up separates stronger-condition onset from transfer at 10/1. The amino-ester outcomes were particularly instructive: m88 needed larger strong-condition completions, but m89 showed an actual small 1/1-to-2/1 decrease. That exception motivates testing the methyl ortho ester and stronger boundaries of other aniline environments. m0 and m5 strong labels were compact and overpredicted at acquisition, and m80's strong pair confirmed compact completion; these results motivate checking current endpoint inversions rather than extending their already covered curves. The m185 lower-loading 1/1 result completed the reference needed after its rejected pure-EA maximum, so no immediate follow-up is allocated there. All stated errors are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The 32 experiments form connected tests of relationships that can generalize across the supplied rows. Strong response-shape experiments extend the latest carbonyl failure repair across aldehydes, fused ketones, a lactone-related structural neighborhood, a beta-diketone and a heteroaromatic ether, while fluorenone and amino esters explicitly test exceptions to a shared compact baseline. The nitrogen comparisons vary amino position and ester versus nitrile connectivity at interpretable strong boundaries. m92 receives two narrowly targeted reference repeats because its latest large miss could otherwise induce an unsupported loading correction; m61 and m72 receive new-condition comparisons that address endpoint-specific and joint recorded-protocol associations. The m83 and m62 loading extremes, m157 solvent pair and m175 strong anchor investigate endpoint coordination where the current predictor gives very narrow or inverted intervals. The chlorobenzophenone pair explores a high-distance weak boundary with meaningful measured structural comparators. Multiple selections on a molecule answer a local curve or loading question, and duplicate catalog predictions are not selected merely to multiply coverage. The expected benefit is improved structure-condition and endpoint learning across the Row-distribution, with recently resolved curves receiving less attention. Loading amount is the supplied density-times-volume feature; no absent concentration, pH, flow or other variables are assumed. Missing experimental factors limit causal attribution. V2 minus V1 is the elution interval width, and quantile spans and CW distance are supplementary signals rather than calibrated epistemic uncertainty. These 32 distinct candidate IDs and their exact associated packet predictions are frozen together before any new measurement reveal.
